Shedding light on one of the many crimes of British. The story doesn't start in India. It begins in Britain, in the slums and streets that bred the Empire's soldiers. For centuries, society was divided into three steps. Those who pray, those who fight and those who work. Most of these commoners lived under debt, unemployment and poverty. Army was your only source of income and also to depopulate the kingdom from the scum of the earth.

Whereas army officers were aristocrats and came from upper classes who were allowed to bring their wives to the colony, a privilege not available for the soldiers. When the Britain took control of India, it designated plots of land called cantonments, away from the general population of India. But there was a problem higher officials feared that isolating these soldiers in cantonment would cause homosexuality amongst them. Else their own high born wives daughters would become a target of their lust.

The British decided to build a system that forced thousands of Indian women into sex slavery. As a solution, and called them "licensed vice" To obtain these women, the police would go into the villages and take from the homes of these poor people, their daughters from 14 years and upwards, and justify it by blaming on their inferior race and giving a better economic opportunity. But in some cases, talking to a man would be enough to denounce her as a prostitute. The British use caste, poverty, chastity or any reasons

available to steal these women from their home. But this was just one of the four stages of the exploitation. In the second stage, they would be provided with a license to solving these jugglers and a fixed price of food on us per visit, cheap enough for every soldier. But these women wouldn't sell 1 or 2 soldiers on a visit for a containment of 10,000 soldiers, 12 to 15 women would be forced to sell.

And the soldiers who were hired from the lower strata of British society would now have a reason to feel superior, and they would demonstrate it by abusing these women. They would be these for men. There would be cuts on arms and breasts, and they would refuse to pay them money and even steal their quilts and sell it to the Indians for a few price, from which they would buy a drink. There were stories about how an angry soldier would set a woman on fire and burn, or alive, and more cruelties,

carrying their anger and rage from their homeland to here and taking it out on someone they believed inferior to them. By the mid 1850s, the British started facing the problems of cities. Around 200 out of 1000 soldiers started suffering from it, and by 1895 it was increased to 500,000 soldiers. But as the same infection rate for Indian troops reached 54 per thousand soldiers. And you know how the British tried to justify that?

They labeled that natives have developed an immunity because of the frequent exposure, and even published an entire scientific journal trying to prove that in 1868, Britishers brought the Contagious Disease Act and administered in India under Cantonment Act, a systemized way to tackle this epidemic. But this act wasn't focused on solving the issue. It was a way to blame Indian women for diseases and a more exploitative way to manage the sex trade. Now, the women entering

these jugglers were first required to go into a local hospital to have their genitalia examined. And this was not a one time visit. Rather a weekly visit where they would go into these hospital and were made sure they don't carry any trace of the diseases which could spread to the soldiers. These lock up hospitals mostly contain inexperienced physicians using vaginal speculum to examine these women, a painful experience as claimed by some escapees.

And if a woman was found to be deceased, she'd be imprisoned in the hospital until she is cured, and if unable to, then she'd be thrown out from this hospital, carrying their half British children hundreds of miles away from their home, along with Indians. British didn't even spare women from their own race. Many Anglo-Indian girls who were left by their father, who left for England were adopted, raised and sent to jail class due to their white skin. Something which was more in demand by the British troops.

Their European and orphan status would be used to keep them in these chocolates, and for the Indian women. They used caste as a justification that these women belonged to the prostitute class anyways. But the authors argued that prostitutes in India one treated as outcasts, they enjoyed a social status. Unlike the prostitutes in Britain. In order to manage and regulate these jugglers, British

would keep Mahal Dannys for a salary of ₹10 a month and would serve to acquire more women and reduce the spread of STDs. Along with your salary, they would also depart from the meager B of the women they would bring in. They would not only deceive the girls into the system, but make sure to not let them escape. And if a woman was caught escaping, she was fined up to ₹50 more than 100 times. Your salary or imprisonment up to seven years.

These Mahal dances would also make sure that the women in charge class would only be available for British troops, and not for native men. And remember, this was a time when British troops were facing high rates of STD diseases. Putting these women under the risk of being captured in local hospitals and faced surgical Ř@pê. In 1895, the Cantonment Act was repealed on the grounds that lock up hospitals and genital examinations of women

have proved to be a failure in controlling the STDs. The general diseases under the context of vice were not to be treated the same as other avoidable contagious diseases, where restriction is necessary to avoid the spread. But just two years later, in 1897, a committee was brought in favor of a return to the system of legalized advice. They argue that because of this 1895 amendment, British troops are suffering from high rates of STDs.

522,000 troops have been removed from active duty, but in reality it was just 43. The 1890 fight, the appeal meant, was led by the efforts of authors which actually worked, decreasing the count. But in order to maintain the system of sex slavery through the efforts of high officials, the system was back up and running. But it was just one year later when this book was published, and the truth was revealed by the book.

And this letter describing the pain, injustice and sin committed under regulations and legislations, seeing this letter sparked a protest in Great Britain and the memorial was signed by 61,000 women against the morality and cruelty of the Cantonment Act. All the reports and findings were submitted in court, and in 1898 only a letter of withdrawal was sent by Lady Henry Somerset to Lord George Hamilton, the same person

who allowed the act to be reinstated in 1897. But it was already too late. Despite the letter being sent and the revelations of truth, the system didn't come to a stop. The exploitation still continued. Women were stolen, used and thrown away as they aged after being removed from chakla’s. The women were never accepted in society as they lived with foreigners. They became the new third state of society. It was in the 1930s when the system was dismantled

after World War-I, which broke the imperial power of the British and the abolitionist movement, asking for the end of every kind of slavery. The British outlawed the prostitution and later left the country while carrying the honor of abolishing sati and child marriage, progressing the Indian society above from stereotypes and castes.
